s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, progressively painful and swelling lesion of the temporal bone
salient_findings: Hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium
Densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone
Low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images with mild patchy internal enhancement
key_facts: 28-year-old man with a history of migraine disorder
Several months of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area
Recent subjective enlargement of the mass and increased pain
Noncontrast CT showed a 3.0 × 3.0 × 1.1 cm hyperostotic lesion
MRI revealed a densely calcified mass measuring 3.6 × 1.5 × 3.0 cm
Thickening of the inner table and no soft-tissue component beyond the bone or dural involvement
Small amount of fluid in the right mastoid air cells and mucosal thickening in the right ethmoid air cells
Laboratory studies, including CBC, BMP, TSH, and free T4, were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: The lesion appeared benign on initial imaging and the patient's symptoms are consistent with a benign bone tumor

shortlist.label: Osteochondroma
shortlist.why_kept: The lesion's location and appearance on MRI are consistent with an osteochondroma, a type of benign bone tumor

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: The densely calcified mass and thickening of the inner table are consistent with an osteoblastoma, a rare benign bone tumor

shortlist.label: Fibrous Dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and the appearance of the lesion on MRI are consistent with fibrous dysplasia, a condition where normal bone is replaced with fibrous tissue

shortlist.label: Chondroma
shortlist.why_kept: The lesion's location and appearance on MRI are consistent with a chondroma, a type of benign cartilaginous tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of a densely calcified mass with low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images and mild patchy internal enhancement, along with the hyperostotic lesion on noncontrast CT, is most consistent with an osteoma, which is a benign bone tumor that can cause localized pain and swelling.

rejected.label: Osteochondroma
rejected.why: Osteochondromas typically have a cartilaginous cap and are more commonly associated with the long bones, which does not match the description of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastomas are typically more aggressive and have a higher signal intensity on T2-weighted images due to their vascular nature, which is not consistent with the imaging findings in this case.

rejected.label: Fibrous Dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia often presents with a ground-glass appearance on imaging and can be associated with laboratory abnormalities, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Chondroma
rejected.why: Chondromas are cartilaginous tumors that are more commonly found in the short tubular bones of the hands and feet, and would not typically present with the imaging characteristics described in this case.
